title: The integers are a G-ring
statement: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07PX, item (3)).

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 07PX (tag 07PX, label proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, line 12652), item (3), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07PX; the proof states that the claim for $\mathbf Z$ follows from the definition and the fact that the completion of a discrete valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring. Proposition 07PX separately cites Proposition 07PS (tag 07PS) for its complete-local-ring item (2).

proof.text: The integers are Noetherian by the standard Mathlib instance. Unfold [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] and fix a prime ideal p. Split into p = 0 and p ≠ 0.

At p = 0, obtain the integer-algebra equivalence of the localization with the rationals from [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr]. Transfer the field property along this equivalence while retaining the existing ring operations. The maximal ideal is zero, so the ring is complete for that ideal. Mathlib AdicCompletion.ofAlgEquiv identifies its canonical completion map with an algebra isomorphism. A bijective algebra map is a localization at the trivial submonoid {1}; apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular] to obtain its regularity.

At p ≠ 0, [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr] supplies the DVR instance. The integer algebra map to the prime localization is injective by its FaithfulSMul instance, so this localization has characteristic zero. Its fraction field has characteristic zero by Mathlib IsFractionRing.charZero_of_isFractionRing. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-completion-regular] with that fraction field.
The two cases prove regularity at every prime; combine this with Noetherianity to conclude IsGRing ℤ.
